title: How to Sell on Instagram Through DMs: 7 Things That Work
summary: Your reels get comments but no sales? Seven things we see in Instagram DMs that sell: free guides, follow-ups, contacts, WhatsApp handoff, a price ladder.
body_markdown:
Your reel got hundreds of comments. A week later you have a long inbox and almost no sales. That's the most common story we hear from creators, coaches and small shops, and it almost never comes from the content. It comes from what happens after the comment.


This autumn we talked with creators, coaches and small shops that use Chatfuel about what happens after the comment, and looked at the public side of their funnels: posts, bios and comments. The accounts that sell do a handful of things differently. Across Chatfuel accounts, those where the AI holds a real conversation get about three times as many replies to the first DM as those that send a link and stop. Here's what the ones that sell do, in the order you'd set it up.


## 1. Think in funnels, not posts


A post doesn't sell. A funnel does: comment, public reply, first DM, the person's reply, a next step, a contact, a sale. Before you write the caption, decide where the sale happens and work back from there.


What you sell decides the shape. The accounts with the most replies sell something people have questions about: a phone on installments, a supplement with delivery, a motorbike with a financing plan. People ask about price, shipping and the down payment, and the DM is the checkout. Experts selling a call or a diagnosis come next. Free material for a keyword gets the fewest replies, because the person already has what they came for.


If you're not sure which funnel fits you, start with[our guide to the three DM funnels for creators](https://chatfuel.com/blog/instagram-dm-funnels-for-creators) : the link funnel, the ladder and the consultation funnel. Then brief your AI the way you'd brief a new salesperson: what you sell, who it's for and what the next step is.


## 2. Give away a lead magnet, and make the first DM do three jobs


Free guides, checklists and quizzes bring the volume. The best first DMs do three things at once: they deliver the guide, connect it to the person's problem, and offer one next step with one easy action. A health and quality-of-life expert sends the guide, adds that if the problem affects daily life it's worth understanding why, offers a personal consultation and asks for a phone number. A doctor sends a ten-question heart-risk quiz with a score and ends with "reply YES and I'll send the five tests to ask your doctor for".


One first DM, three jobs: the guide, the problem, one next step


That last line matters. Instagram lets you send a new contact only one DM after a comment until they reply ([messaging rules](https://chatfuel.com/docs/instagram/messaging-rules-for-instagram) ). A reply opens the conversation, so the next resource and the offer can follow. And in the[public reply](https://chatfuel.com/comments-replies) , tell people to check their message requests: if they don't follow you, that's where your DM lands.


## 3. Follow up after the lead magnet


The most valuable messages in a chat arrive after the link: a phone number, a question about the product, a detailed story about the person's situation that ends with "what do you suggest?". Often nobody answers them, because the conversation stops after the first message, or the AI doesn't know what the account sells.


The question that matters arrives after the link


- Keep the conversation on after the first DM, and tell the AI what comes after the free thing.
- [Turn on follow-ups for people who go quiet](https://chatfuel.com/follow-ups) inside the 24-hour window.
- Use a reply word to chain resources: guide, "reply WORD for part two", part two, the offer.


**In Chatfuel:** when someone writes back after a comment, the comment automation keeps answering them in DMs for about a day ([how it works](https://chatfuel.com/docs/instagram/instagram-comment-autoreply#which-rule-answers-a-comment) ). Make sure its **Incoming messages** isn't set to **Don't reply** , describe the next step in **Additional instructions** , and turn on[Follow-ups](https://chatfuel.com/docs/ai-features/how-to-set-up-follow-ups) for people who go quiet.


## 4. Collect data, and build an asset you own


Instagram only lets you talk inside a window. A contact lets you come back. Ask for it as the way to receive something ("Where should I send the checklist?"), and[ask two or three questions that tell you who's ready](https://chatfuel.com/lead-qualification) : goal, timing, budget, city.


This is the part most people underestimate. A list of people who asked about your offer, with what they want and how to reach them, is one of the most valuable things your Instagram produces. They aren't followers who scrolled past. They're interested leads who told you what they need. That list is yours: you can come back to it with a launch, a new product or an invitation, in DMs, on WhatsApp or by email, long after the post is forgotten.


A common leak: sending people to a quiz on a website that asks the same questions the AI just asked. Ask in the chat, once, and pass the answers on.


**In Chatfuel:** turn on[Collect contact info](https://chatfuel.com/docs/ai-features/how-to-collect-contact-info) and list the fields you need (phone, email, city, budget); they land on the contact card in **Leads** . Describe who counts as a good lead in **Additional instructions** , and watch them move from Captured leads to Qualified leads on the[Leads board](https://chatfuel.com/docs/leads/leads) .


Those contacts are yours to use. Ask the AI Co-Worker to connect Google Sheets, HubSpot or another tool and send them there, or take them out through the[Public API](https://chatfuel.com/docs/public-api/overview) .


## 5. Hand off from Instagram to WhatsApp with context, not into silence


For many small businesses WhatsApp is where the sale closes. It's also where leads often die: the AI sends a link to the owner's personal WhatsApp, the owner is busy, and nobody answers.


- Hand off at a clear moment: ready to buy, a question only a human can answer, a problem after purchase.
- If people type a word like "advisor" to reach a person,[make it a real handoff](https://chatfuel.com/live-chat) with a notification, not an AI that goes quiet.
- Better still, connect WhatsApp to the same AI, so the conversation continues with the same history instead of starting over.


**In Chatfuel:** set **Switch to human** on the automation with your own conditions,[customize the handoff message](https://chatfuel.com/docs/ai-features/can-i-customize-the-handoff-message) , and connect WhatsApp to the same AI.


## 6. Build a price ladder, and stay in touch between steps


The accounts that earn the most from DMs don't jump from free to expensive. They put a small paid step in between:


Step What it is What we saw


Free Guide, checklist, quiz, recipe Brings the comments and the first reply


Low-ticket A paid diagnosis, a short personal consultation, a starter pack, a supplement The first purchase; it qualifies the person


Core Program, challenge, course, treatment Recommended by the AI based on what the person said


Recurring Membership, monthly group session, refills Offered after the core purchase


A small paid step before the big one


A psychologist starts with a paid diagnostic session and[recommends the right program after it](https://chatfuel.com/cross-sell-and-upsell) . A real estate educator asks which strategy interests you and recommends the matching ticket of his challenge. Steps that take days need a way to reach people again, because Instagram only lets you write within 24 hours of their last message. Collect a WhatsApp number or an email and use it for reminders before a launch, a check-in after the free guide, a reminder the day before the call. On WhatsApp, messages outside the 24-hour window go out as[approved templates](https://chatfuel.com/whatsapp-templates) .


## 7. Watch your chats, and let AI help


The dashboard can look great while the funnel leaks. Once a week, open the chats:


- **Unanswered after the link.** Look for chats where the customer wrote last.
- **Stages that lie.** A lead closed as won where the AI only sent a payment link isn't a sale.
- **Limits.** If your plan hits its conversation limit, replies can stop. Watch the limit warnings in your account before a launch.
- **Messages that need a human.** Health symptoms, complaints, personal messages from friends.
- **Replies from the Instagram app.** When you answer from the Instagram app, automation pauses for that chat. Make Fuely AI the assignee again, or set a chat timeout so the chat comes back on its own.


You don't have to do this by hand. With the[Chatfuel MCP](https://chatfuel.com/docs/mcp) , you can connect your Chatfuel account to Claude, ChatGPT or another AI assistant and ask in plain words: summarize last week's chats, find the customers nobody answered, spot the questions your AI can't answer yet, add those answers to its FAQ and instructions, and set up comment replies on the posts you choose. Fuely runs the conversations; the MCP lets you manage Fuely the same way.


One request: the chats nobody answered, and what to add to the FAQ


## Checklist


- Decide where the sale happens and work back to the post
- Brief the AI like a new salesperson: what you sell, for whom, the next step
- "Check your message requests" in the public reply
- First DM: the free thing, the problem, one next step
- Conversation and follow-ups on after the first DM
- Contact and two or three qualifying questions in the chat, saved where you can use them later
- Handoff with context; WhatsApp on the same AI
- A low-ticket step between free and core
- A weekly look at the chats


## FAQs


### Why do people comment but not buy?


Usually because the conversation ends after the first DM. The questions that lead to a sale come after the link, and nobody answers them.


### Should my first DM include the link?


Yes, along with a reason to reply: one question or one next step. A reply opens the 24-hour window for the rest of the conversation.


### When should I move a lead to WhatsApp?


When the next steps take days (a launch, a booking, a delivery) or need a human. Pass the context along, and if you can, run the same AI there.


### Can I take my leads to my own CRM?


Yes. The contacts the AI collects stay on their cards in Leads, and you can send them to Google Sheets, HubSpot or another CRM: ask the AI Co-Worker to connect it, or use the Public API.


### What should I sell between a free guide and my main program?


A small paid step that helps the person and tells you what they need: a diagnosis, a short consultation, a starter pack.
